Synopsis:
Canada's ambassador to Washington states that any US-Canada trade deal must preserve a viable Canadian auto assembly and parts industry as a non-negotiable condition. Talks collapsed after Trump imposed 50% tariffs on $20B of Canadian goods, with Canada retaliating with its own $20B in tariffs effective September 8. Key sticking point: tariff treatment of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles. Both sides signal continued willingness to negotiate but no resumption date is set. Canada states all options remain open.
